grade.first_issue: In the sufficiency argument for k≥3, the claim that every open interval of length at least θ contains a multiple of θ is false when its length is exactly θ and its endpoints are consecutive multiples. Here the only problematic case is k=3 and α=60°, which forces the triangle to be equilateral and hence already terminal. Adding this case split repairs the proof directly; no Rule A–F ceiling applies.
grade.summary: The classification θ=180°/k for integers k≥2 is correct. The angle-peeling induction and the safe-state invariant in the necessity direction are sound. Apart from a minor endpoint oversight in the interval argument, the proof establishes both directions.
strengths: Correctly shows that an angle nθ can be reduced to θ by repeatedly splitting off θ.
Provides a valid one-cut construction placing supplementary multiples of θ in the two child triangles.
Correctly enumerates the four ways both children could contain multiples of θ and derives a contradiction, yielding Shan-Yu's invariant strategy.
Reaches the complete and correct classification.

errors.description: The open-interval lattice-point assertion overlooks the equality case; this is harmless after explicitly separating triangles already containing an angle in W.
The existence of an initial triangle with no angle in W is asserted without an example. It is routine: the equilateral triangle works, since 60°=nθ would imply 180°=3nθ.
